name: Exemptions

subjectOf.text: Because Title IV's registration exemptions are broad enough to threaten the rule they qualify, the Dodd-Frank Act deliberately gives the SEC rulemaking authority to keep the exemptions from swallowing the rules.
subjectOf.abstract: The Dodd-Frank Act also empowers the SEC to utilize its rulemaking authority to prevent the exemptions from registration to "swallow the rules."100
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Hedge Fund Manager Registration Under the Dodd-Frank Act (2012). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2150377
scope_conditions: exemptions for private fund advisers, venture capital advisers, and foreign private advisers under Title IV

subjectOf.text: The Jumpstart Our Business Startups Act exemptions for emerging growth companies from Section 404(b), from say-on-pay, and from pay ratio disclosure illustrate the post-crisis easing of constraints imposed on the financial services industry.
subjectOf.abstract: These exemptions again illustrate the easing of constraints imposed on the financial services industry after a crisis.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Dynamic Regulation of the Financial Services Industry (2013). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2273857
scope_conditions: emerging growth companies under the JOBS Act

subjectOf.text: Title IV requires private fund advisers with more than $150 million in assets under management to register with the SEC as investment advisers.
subjectOf.abstract: Title IV requires private fund advisers with more than $150 million assets under management (AUM) to register with the SEC as investment advisers.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The Private Fund Industry Five Years after the Dodd-Frank Act – A Survey Study (2016). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2732915
scope_conditions: advisers acting solely as advisers to private funds
assets under management in the United States
